review_notes:
I read all of Rotation.lean (lines 1–135). I also read the upstream simp lemmas it uses: coe_spinRotation, spinRotation_zero and spinRotation_pi in the linear-algebra Rotation file; realCliffordForm_apply, realCliffordForm_apply_single and realCliffordForm_zero_single_one; realCliffordSpinInclusion_negOne; and Mathlib's Pi.basisFun_apply.

The only simp attribute added here is `spinRotationPath_apply`. It rewrites the bundled path evaluation to `spinRotation … (π * t)`, which is a sensible direction: it terminates, and the upstream endpoint lemmas spinRotation_zero and spinRotation_pi are already @[simp]. I found no competing rules and no cycle risk.

The repeated `simpa only [Pi.basisFun_apply] using realCliffordForm_zero_single_one …` appears four times (lines 103, 105, 116, 117). Pi.basisFun_apply and realCliffordForm_zero_single_one are both already @[simp], so plain `simp` already covers this. A new simp lemma would be redundant.

The `Nat.add_assoc` and `Nat.reduceAdd` rewriting in the final induction step (lines 130–131) is a proof-local index normalisation, not a defect in the simp set. I found no justified simp-interface change.
